s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic inflammatory condition of the nails and mucosa with potential systemic involvement
salient_findings: Painful swelling of the proximal nail folds
Dripping of blood from fingernails and toenails
Occasional pus discharge
Lichenoid plaques and erosions on the oral mucosa
Violaceous discoloration and longitudinal ridging of the nails
key_facts: Male patient in his 60s
Symptoms present for the last year
No history of preceding trauma or drug intake
Raised liver enzyme levels
Positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status
Hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, and basal cell degeneration on histopathology
Numerous apoptotic keratinocytes in the epidermis
Dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis
Partial to complete loss of nail plate with oozing of blood and hemorrhagic crusting

differentials: Nail lichen planus with hepatitis C
per_call: Nail lichen planus with hepatitis C

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of painful swelling of the proximal nail folds, violaceous discoloration, and histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, and basal cell degeneration

shortlist.label: Hepatitis C-associated lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status and raised liver enzyme levels, suggesting a potential link between hepatitis C and lichen planus

shortlist.label: Psoriatic nail disease
shortlist.why_kept: Nail changes such as longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation of the nail plate, which can be seen in psoriatic nail disease

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of lichenoid plaques on the oral mucosa and erosions covered with hemorrhagic crusts, which can be seen in dermatomyositis

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Mucosal involvement and potential systemic symptoms, which can be seen in lupus erythematosus

raw.rationale: The patient's positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status, raised liver enzyme levels, and histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, basal cell degeneration, and dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate are consistent with lichen planus, and the association with hepatitis C virus infection supports this specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: While the histopathological findings are consistent with lichen planus, the presence of hepatitis C virus infection suggests a more specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Psoriatic nail disease
rejected.why: The lack of characteristic psoriatic nail changes such as pitting, onycholysis, or oil drop discoloration, and the presence of lichenoid plaques and erosions on the oral mucosa, make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: The absence of characteristic dermatomyositis features such as Gottron's papules, heliotrope rash, or muscle weakness, and the presence of lichenoid plaques and nail changes, make this diagnosis unlikely

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The lack of characteristic lupus erythematosus features such as malar rash, discoid lesions, or systemic symptoms, and the presence of lichenoid plaques and nail changes, make this diagnosis unlikely
